hypotheses.reason: SAHA inhibits HDAC catalytic activity, raising acetylation and potentially altering transcription; direction per gene is unknown.
Enzyme inhibition does not imply lowered mRNA; HDAC transcript changes are secondary and unmeasured.
These are abundant in untreated A549; HDAC inhibition may perturb stress programs but direction is unsupported.
Chromatin changes could indirectly affect metabolic transcription; no measured signature supports a direction.

summary: SAHA directly inhibits HDAC catalytic activity, plausibly increasing acetylation-linked transcription, but specific gene directions in A549 at 5 uM/24 h are unmeasured and uncertain.
limitations: No measured treatment response or dose trajectory provided.
Isoform engagement and homologue-based structural evidence limit inference.
Per-gene transcriptional direction from HDAC inhibition is context dependent.
